examples.en: My great-grandfather is ninety this year.

examples.ko: 명절에는 온 가족이 증조할아버지 댁에 모여요.
examples.en: On holidays the whole family gathers at my great-grandfather's house.
My great-grandfather told us stories from the old days.

examples.ko: 저는 증조할아버지를 한 번도 만나 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never met my great-grandfather.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 증조할아버지가 젊었을 때 찍은 거예요.
examples.en: This photo was taken when my great-grandfather was young.
My great-grandfather and great-grandmother farmed in their hometown.

explain: 윗사람이라서 '이/가' 대신 '께서'를 쓰고, '먹다'는 '드시다'처럼 높여 말해요. 어머니의 할아버지는 보통 '외증조할아버지'라고 해요. 짝말은 '증조할머니'예요.
explain_en: Because he is an elder, use '께서' instead of '이/가' and honorific verbs like '드시다' for 'eat'. Your mother's grandfather is usually called '외증조할아버지'. The female counterpart is '증조할머니'.

examples.en: The one who is always late in our class is Minsu.
I ended up being a latecomer again today.
The teacher made the latecomers clean the classroom.
Latecomers, please come in through the front door.
These days the number of latecomers has dropped a lot.

examples.ko: 지각생에서 벗어나려고 일찍 일어나는 연습을 해요.
examples.en: I am practicing getting up early to stop being the latecomer.

explain: 주로 학교에서 쓰는 말이고, 지각을 자주 하는 학생을 가리켜요. 친구끼리는 놀리는 말투로도 쓰니까 어른에게는 '지각을 자주 하시는 분'처럼 돌려 말하는 게 좋아요. '지각하다'가 동사예요.
explain_en: It is mostly a school word for students who are often late. Friends also use it teasingly, so with adults it is better to say something like '지각을 자주 하시는 분'. The verb form is '지각하다'.

examples.en: There is a small globe on the desk.

examples.ko: 지구본을 돌리면서 가고 싶은 나라를 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: I spun the globe and looked for countries I want to visit.
I bought a globe as a birthday present for my child.

examples.ko: 지구본으로 보면 한국과 브라질이 얼마나 먼지 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: On a globe you can see how far apart Korea and Brazil are.

examples.ko: 지구본은 세계 지도보다 실제 모양에 더 가까워요.
examples.en: A globe is closer to the real shape than a world map.
Shall we try finding our country on this globe?

explain: 평평한 '세계 지도'와 달리 둥근 모양이라 나라의 크기와 거리를 더 실제에 가깝게 볼 수 있어요. 보통 '지구본을 돌리다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike a flat '세계 지도' (world map), the round shape shows country sizes and distances closer to reality. The usual collocation is '지구본을 돌리다' (to spin the globe).

examples.en: Lots of cars pass along this road.

examples.ko: 아침마다 이 골목을 지나다니는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people pass through this alley every morning.

examples.ko: 매일 그 가게 앞을 지나다녔는데 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I passed by that shop every day but never noticed it.

examples.ko: 버스가 자주 지나다니는 길이라서 좀 시끄러워요.
examples.en: It is a road buses often pass along, so it is a bit noisy.
Drive slowly where children walk by.
I heard that long ago cows used to pass along this road.

explain: '지나가다'는 한 번 지나가는 것이고, '지나다니다'는 같은 곳을 자주 오가는 느낌이에요. '길을 지나다니다'나 '이 길로 지나다니다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '지나가다' is passing once, while '지나다니다' means going back and forth past the same place often. You can say '길을 지나다니다' or '이 길로 지나다니다'.

examples.en: I took an express bus from Seoul to Busan.
The express bus hardly stops on the way.
Please check the express bus timetable.

examples.ko: 이 직행버스는 한 시간에 한 대 있어요.
examples.en: This express bus runs once an hour.
It takes about two hours by express bus.
The express bus is a bit more expensive than a regular bus.

explain: 서는 곳이 많은 '완행'과 대비해서 써요. 터미널에서는 '직행으로 한 장 주세요'처럼 줄여서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It contrasts with '완행', which stops at many places. At a terminal people often shorten it, saying '직행으로 한 장 주세요' (One express ticket, please).

examples.en: I put two spoonfuls of jin-ganjang into the bulgogi.

examples.ko: 진간장이 다 떨어져서 마트에 가야 해요.
examples.en: We ran out of jin-ganjang, so I have to go to the mart.
It is better to use jin-ganjang for braised dishes.
Mix jin-ganjang and sugar to make the sauce.

examples.ko: 이 진간장은 색이 진하고 맛이 깊어요.
examples.en: This jin-ganjang is dark and has a deep flavor.

examples.ko: 볶음밥에 진간장을 조금만 넣어도 맛이 확 살아요.
examples.en: Just a little jin-ganjang makes fried rice taste much better.

explain: 국이나 나물을 무칠 때 쓰는 '국간장'과 구분해요. 진간장은 조림, 볶음, 불고기처럼 색과 단맛이 필요한 요리에 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is distinguished from '국간장', used for soups and seasoned vegetables. Jin-ganjang is commonly used in braised, stir-fried and bulgogi-type dishes where color and sweetness matter.

examples.en: The nurse showed me to the examination room.
I waited in front of the examination room to be called.

examples.ko: 진찰실에 들어가면 의사 선생님께 증상을 말씀드리세요.
examples.en: When you go into the examination room, tell the doctor your symptoms.
The child cried in the examination room because she was scared.

examples.ko: 이 병원은 진찰실이 세 개 있어요.
examples.en: This clinic has three examination rooms.

examples.ko: 진찰실은 이 층 복도 끝에 있어요.
examples.en: The examination room is at the end of the hallway on the second floor.

explain: 병원에서 의사가 환자를 보는 방이고, 수술하는 '수술실'이나 약을 받는 '약국'과 달라요. 말할 때는 그냥 '안으로 들어가세요'라고도 많이 해요.
explain_en: It is the room where a doctor sees patients, different from '수술실' (operating room) or '약국' (pharmacy). In speech, staff often just say '안으로 들어가세요' (please go inside).

examples.ko: 아빠가 차 짐칸에 큰 가방을 실었어요.
examples.en: Dad loaded the big bag into the cargo area of the car.
Please unload the boxes from the truck bed.

examples.ko: 버스 짐칸에 캐리어를 넣고 자리에 앉았어요.
examples.en: I put my suitcase in the bus luggage compartment and sat down.
The cargo space is small, so the stroller does not fit.
It is dangerous for children to ride in the back of a truck.

examples.ko: 출발하기 전에 짐칸 문이 잘 닫혔는지 확인했어요.
examples.en: Before leaving, I checked that the cargo door was closed properly.

explain: 승용차 뒤쪽은 '트렁크'라고 많이 말하고, 트럭이나 버스처럼 짐을 싣는 칸은 '짐칸'이라고 해요. '짐을 싣다/내리다'와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: For a passenger car's rear, people often say '트렁크', while '짐칸' is the cargo space of a truck, bus and similar vehicles. It often appears with '짐을 싣다/내리다' (load/unload).

examples.ko: 집배원이 등기를 가져왔는데 집에 아무도 없어서 못 받았어요.
examples.en: The mail carrier brought a registered letter, but nobody was home so I could not receive it.
I handed the letter to the mail carrier.
Mail carriers deliver mail even when it rains.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 집배원은 늘 인사를 잘해요.
examples.en: The mail carrier in our neighborhood always greets us nicely.

examples.ko: 집배원이 초인종을 눌러서 문을 열어 줬어요.
examples.en: The mail carrier rang the doorbell, so I opened the door.

examples.ko: 어머니는 집배원으로 십 년 넘게 일하셨어요.
examples.en: My mother worked as a mail carrier for over ten years.

explain: 직접 부를 때는 '집배원 아저씨/아주머니'라고 해요. '우체부'라고도 하는데 '집배원'이 지금 더 공식적인 말이에요. 일하는 곳은 '우체국'이에요.
explain_en: When addressing one directly, say '집배원 아저씨/아주머니'. '우체부' is also used, but '집배원' is the more official term now. They work at a '우체국' (post office).

examples.en: My deskmate is very tall.
I did the homework together with my deskmate.
I am happy to have a new deskmate.
I borrowed an eraser from my deskmate.
The teacher chose our deskmates by drawing lots.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 짝꿍이랑 계속 이야기해서 혼났어요.
examples.en: I got scolded for talking with my deskmate all through class.

explain: 학교에서 옆자리에 앉은 친구를 말해서 초등학생이 특히 많이 써요. 어른들끼리는 보통 '짝'이나 '단짝'이라고 하고, '짝꿍'은 친한 친구나 파트너를 귀엽게 부를 때도 써요.
explain_en: It means the classmate who sits next to you, and elementary students use it a lot. Adults usually say '짝' or '단짝', though '짝꿍' can also affectionately mean a close friend or partner.

examples.en: I ate jjolmyeon with a friend for lunch.
Jjolmyeon is sweet, sour and spicy.
Excuse me, one jjolmyeon, please.
We ordered jjolmyeon and gimbap at the snack restaurant.
Please put lots of vegetables in my jjolmyeon.

examples.ko: 쫄면은 면이 쫄깃해서 먹을 때 재미있어요.
examples.en: The noodles in jjolmyeon are chewy, so it is fun to eat.

explain: 분식집에서 많이 파는 메뉴예요. 라면이나 냉면과 달리 면이 굵고 쫄깃하고, 매콤새콤한 양념에 비벼 먹어요.
explain_en: It is a common menu item at snack restaurants. Unlike ramyeon or naengmyeon, the noodles are thick and chewy, and you mix them with a spicy-sour sauce.

examples.ko: 살을 찌우려고 하루에 네 끼씩 먹어요.
examples.en: I eat four meals a day to gain weight.
My younger brother wants to put on weight.

examples.ko: 겨울이 오기 전에 살을 좀 찌웠어요.
examples.en: I gained some weight before winter came.

examples.ko: 살을 찌우는 것보다 빼는 게 더 어려워요.
examples.en: Losing weight is harder than gaining it.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 살을 조금 찌우라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to put on a little weight.

examples.ko: 아기 고양이를 잘 먹여서 살을 찌웠어요.
examples.en: I fed the kitten well and fattened it up.

explain: '살이 찌다'는 저절로 살이 오르는 것이고, '살을 찌우다'는 일부러 살을 늘리거나 누군가를 살찌게 하는 거예요. 반대로 살을 줄일 때는 '살을 빼다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '살이 찌다' is gaining weight on its own, while '살을 찌우다' is deliberately gaining weight or making someone gain it. The opposite is '살을 빼다' (lose weight).

examples.en: The teacher shouted 'Attention!' in a loud voice.

examples.ko: 교장 선생님이 오시자 반장이 '차렷!' 하고 말했어요.
examples.en: When the principal came, the class president said 'Attention!'

examples.ko: 모두 차렷 자세로 똑바로 서 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone is standing straight in the attention posture.

examples.ko: 차렷 하면 팔을 몸 옆에 붙이세요.
examples.en: When I say 'attention', keep your arms at your sides.

examples.ko: 아이들이 차렷 하고 서서 국기에 인사해요.
examples.en: The children stand at attention and salute the flag.

examples.ko: 군인처럼 차렷 하고 섰더니 친구들이 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friends laughed when I stood at attention like a soldier.

explain: 학교나 군대에서 쓰는 구령이에요. 보통 '차렷, 경례' 순서로 이어지고, 편하게 서라고 할 때는 '쉬어'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a command used at school and in the military. It usually comes in the order '차렷, 경례' (attention, salute), and '쉬어' means stand at ease.

examples.en: Please line up and go in one at a time.
The children got on the bus one after another.
I checked the documents one by one.
The guests arrived one after another.
The names were called one by one in number order.

examples.ko: 일이 많을 때는 차례차례 하나씩 끝내세요.
examples.en: When you have a lot of work, finish it one thing at a time.

explain: '순서대로'는 정해진 순서를 따른다는 점이 중심이고, '차례차례'는 하나가 끝나면 다음이 이어지는 모습을 그려요. '한꺼번에'와 반대로 쓰여요.
explain_en: '순서대로' stresses following a set order, while '차례차례' paints one thing following another. It is used as the opposite of '한꺼번에' (all at once).

examples.en: I bought two tickets at the ticket office.
I lost my ticket, so I bought another.
Please show your ticket to the driver.
How much is one ticket?
You have to buy holiday tickets early.
I booked the ticket in advance.

explain: 버스나 기차 같은 탈것의 표를 넓게 말해요. 어떤 차인지 분명히 할 때는 '버스표', '기차표'라고 해요.
explain_en: It broadly means a ticket for a bus, train or similar vehicle. When you want to be specific, say '버스표' or '기차표'.

examples.en: If there is cold rice, I make fried rice.
I heat cold rice in the microwave before eating.
I ate the leftover cold rice from the morning for lunch.
I made porridge with cold rice.

examples.ko: 찬밥이 싫으면 따뜻한 밥을 새로 지을게요.
examples.en: If you do not like cold rice, I will cook fresh rice.

examples.ko: 냄비에 찬밥 한 공기가 남아 있어요.
examples.en: There is a bowl of cold rice left in the pot.

explain: '식은 밥'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 반대는 '따뜻한 밥'이나 '더운밥'이에요. 식은 밥으로 볶음밥이나 죽을 많이 만들어요.

phrases.example: 새 직원이 들어오자 그는 찬밥 신세가 됐어요.
phrases.en: When a new employee joined, he was left out in the cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸모없다고 여겨져 푸대접을 받는 처지를 말해요. 주로 불만이나 서운함을 담아 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone treated as useless and neglected. It usually carries a tone of complaint or hurt.
phrases.en_equiv: be left out in the cold

explain_en: It means almost the same as '식은 밥', and the opposite is '따뜻한 밥' or '더운밥'. Cold rice is often used to make fried rice or porridge.

examples.en: Cold rain has been falling since morning, so I took an umbrella.

examples.ko: 찬비를 맞았더니 감기에 걸린 것 같아요.
examples.en: I got caught in the cold rain, so I think I caught a cold.

examples.ko: 찬비에 옷이 다 젖어서 집에 일찍 갔어요.
examples.en: My clothes got soaked in the cold rain, so I went home early.
People kept walking hard even in the cold rain.
I can hear the cold rain falling outside the window.

examples.ko: 찬비가 그치면 날씨가 더 추워질 거예요.
examples.en: Once the cold rain stops, the weather will get even colder.

explain: '찬'은 '차다'의 관형형이라서 '찬비'는 '차가운 비'와 거의 같아요. 대화에서는 '비가 차요'나 '차가운 비'처럼 말하는 경우도 많고, '찬비'는 글이나 노래에서 분위기를 살릴 때 잘 어울려요. 늦가을이나 겨울 앞의 쌀쌀한 비를 떠올리게 해요.
explain_en: '찬' is the modifier form of '차다' (to be cold), so '찬비' is almost the same as '차가운 비'. In conversation people often say '비가 차요' or '차가운 비', while '찬비' fits writing and songs where you want a mood. It brings to mind chilly rain in late autumn or just before winter.

examples.en: Many participating nations gather at the Olympics.

examples.ko: 이번 대회의 참가국은 모두 서른 나라예요.
examples.en: There are thirty participating countries in this tournament in total.
Each participating country has a different cheering culture, so it's fun.
The organizers announced the participating countries.
Korea is also included among the participating nations of this event.
Representatives of the participating countries gathered in the meeting room.

explain: 대회나 회의, 행사에 나오는 나라를 말할 때 써요. 대회를 여는 나라는 '개최국'이나 '주최국'이라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. 뉴스와 스포츠 기사에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: Use it for the countries that take part in a competition, meeting or event. The country that hosts it is called '개최국' or '주최국', so it helps to learn them as a pair. You will often see it in news and sports articles.

examples.ko: 서점에서 수학 참고서를 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a math reference book at the bookstore.
I marked the parts I did not understand in the study guide.
I inherited the study guide my older brother used.
This study guide is good because the explanations are easy.
Please use the textbook and the study guide together.
I have so many study guides that my bag is heavy.

explain: 학교에서 쓰는 '교과서'를 보충해 주는 공부 책이에요. 문제를 많이 푸는 책은 보통 '문제집'이라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It is a study book that supplements the school '교과서' (textbook). A book mainly full of practice problems is usually called a '문제집' instead.

examples.en: The windowpane is broken, so wind comes in.
A ball flew over and nearly broke the windowpane.
In winter, steam fogs up the windowpane.
I brought a rag to clean the windowpanes.
This house is quiet because the windowpanes are thick.
I can hear raindrops hitting the windowpane.

explain: 창문에 끼워진 유리 그 자체를 가리켜요. 창문 전체를 말할 때는 '유리창'이라고도 하는데, 깨지거나 닦거나 두께를 말할 때는 '창유리'가 잘 맞아요. '창유리가 깨지다', '창유리를 닦다'처럼 함께 써요.
explain_en: It points to the glass itself that is set in a window. For the whole window you can also say '유리창', but '창유리' fits when talking about breaking, cleaning or thickness. It goes with phrases like '창유리가 깨지다' and '창유리를 닦다'.

examples.en: A lot of dust has piled up on the window frame.
When it rains, water collects in the window frame.
The cat is sitting on the window sill.
I brought a rag to wipe the window frame.
The window frame is old, so the wind comes in.
I put the flowerpot on the window ledge.

explain: 유리가 아니라 창을 둘러싼 틀 부분이에요. 대청소할 때 '창틀 청소'가 힘들다는 말을 많이 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the frame around the window, not the glass. People often say that cleaning the window frames is the hard part of a big clean.

examples.en: Grandmother is picking lettuce in the vegetable garden.

examples.ko: 우리 집 뒤에 작은 채소밭이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small vegetable garden behind our house.
I water the vegetable garden every weekend.
We grow peppers and tomatoes in the vegetable garden.
Lots of weeds have grown in the vegetable garden.

examples.ko: 채소밭은 햇볕이 잘 드는 곳이 좋아요.
examples.en: A vegetable garden should be in a sunny spot.

explain: 집 가까이에 작게 가꾸는 밭은 '텃밭'이라고 많이 해요. '채소밭'은 크기와 상관없이 채소를 기르는 밭이라는 점이 중심이에요. '밭을 갈다', '채소를 키우다'와 자주 함께 써요.
explain_en: A small plot grown near the house is often called a '텃밭'. '채소밭' focuses on the fact that vegetables are grown there, regardless of size. It pairs well with '밭을 갈다' (to plow) and '채소를 키우다' (to grow vegetables).

examples.en: This temple was built a thousand years ago.
It is a city with a thousand years of history.
They say that tree has lived for a thousand years.

examples.ko: 천년이 지나도 이 노래는 기억될 거예요.
examples.en: Even after a thousand years, this song will be remembered.
It's special because it's a tradition that has lasted a thousand years.

examples.ko: 천년 전 사람들도 별을 보며 길을 찾았어요.
examples.en: People a thousand years ago also found their way by looking at the stars.

explain: 맞춤법으로는 '천 년'처럼 띄어 쓰는 경우가 많고, '수천 년'은 '몇천 년'의 뜻으로 써요. 정확히 1000년이라기보다 '아주 오랜 시간'을 말할 때도 많아요. 비슷한 말로 '오랜 세월'이 있어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 정말 오랫동안이라는 뜻으로 과장해서 말할 때 써요. 보통 '살다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: An exaggeration meaning for a very, very long time. It usually appears with verbs like '살다' (to live).

explain_en: In standard spelling it is often written with a space, '천 년', and '수천 년' means several thousand years. It is often used for 'a very long time' rather than exactly 1,000 years. A similar expression is '오랜 세월' (long years).

examples.ko: 자리를 비울 때 모니터를 끄는 것이 사무실 절전의 첫걸음이에요.
examples.en: Turning off the monitor when you leave your seat is the first step to saving power in the office.

examples.ko: 한국어 공부의 첫걸음은 한글을 읽는 거예요.
examples.en: The first step in studying Korean is reading Hangul.
The baby finally took her first steps.

examples.ko: 새로운 일을 시작할 때는 첫걸음이 가장 어려워요.
examples.en: When starting something new, the first step is the hardest.

examples.ko: 이 만남이 우리 협력의 첫걸음이 되길 바라요.
examples.en: I hope this meeting becomes the first step of our cooperation.

examples.ko: 작은 습관 하나가 건강한 생활의 첫걸음이 돼요.
examples.en: One small habit becomes the first step to a healthy life.

explain: 아기의 첫 걸음처럼 실제 걸음에도 쓰고, 어떤 일의 시작이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. '첫걸음을 떼다'나 '첫걸음을 내딛다'로 자주 말하고, 비슷한 말로 '첫발'이 있어요.
explain_en: It can mean a baby's actual first steps, but it is also widely used figuratively for the start of something. People often say '첫걸음을 떼다' or '첫걸음을 내딛다', and '첫발' is a similar word.

examples.en: I was the first daughter, so my parents were very happy.
My friend gave birth to her first daughter last week.
Our first daughter has already become an elementary school student.
We thought for a long time before naming our first daughter.
The first daughter in our house is my older sister.

examples.ko: 첫딸을 키울 때는 모든 게 처음이라 힘들었어요.
examples.en: Raising our first daughter was hard because everything was new.

explain: 딸 중에서 첫째 딸은 '맏딸'이고, '첫딸'은 처음 낳은 딸을 말할 때 많이 써요. 비슷하게 '첫아들', '첫아이'도 있어요.
explain_en: '맏딸' is the eldest of the daughters, while '첫딸' is often used for the first daughter a parent has. Similar words are '첫아들' and '첫아이'.

examples.en: Cheonggukjang has a strong smell but tastes good.
I cooked cheonggukjang stew for dinner.
I add tofu and kimchi to the cheonggukjang.

examples.ko: 청국장을 먹고 나서 창문을 열어 환기했어요.
examples.en: After eating cheonggukjang, I opened the window to air out the room.
I tried cheonggukjang for the first time and it tasted nutty.
Cheonggukjang and a bowl of rice, please.

explain: 된장찌개와 비슷하게 끓여 먹지만 냄새가 훨씬 강해서 호불호가 갈려요. 식당에서는 '청국장찌개'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is boiled like doenjang jjigae, but the smell is much stronger, so people either love it or dislike it. In restaurants it may be called '청국장찌개'.

examples.en: The sea shines blue-green.
I bought a blue-green shirt.

examples.ko: 저는 청록색이 잘 어울린다는 말을 자주 들어요.
examples.en: I often hear that blue-green suits me.

examples.ko: 청록색 커튼으로 바꾸니까 방 분위기가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: The room feels different after I changed to blue-green curtains.

examples.ko: 청록색 물감이 없어서 파랑과 초록을 섞었어요.
examples.en: I had no turquoise paint, so I mixed blue and green.

examples.ko: 이 호수는 날씨에 따라 청록색을 띠어요.
examples.en: This lake looks blue-green depending on the weather.

explain: '청록색'만 쓰기도 하고 '청록'이라고만 줄여 말하기도 해요. '민트색'은 더 연하고 밝은 색을 말할 때 쓰는 편이에요. '색을 띠다'와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: You can say '청록색' or shorten it to just '청록'. '민트색' tends to be used for a lighter, brighter shade. It often appears with '색을 띠다' (to take on a color).

examples.en: Green grapes are sweet and sour.
I bought a bunch of green grapes at the market.
I washed the green grapes and put them in the fridge.
I ordered a green grape ade at the cafe.

examples.ko: 이 청포도는 씨가 없어서 먹기 편해요.
examples.en: These green grapes have no seeds, so they are easy to eat.
My child likes green grapes, so I buy them often.

explain: 보라색 포도와 구분해서 초록색 포도를 말할 때 써요. 껍질째 먹는 경우가 많고, 음료나 케이크 이름에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It distinguishes green grapes from the purple kind. They are often eaten with the skin, and the name often appears in drinks and cakes.

examples.en: We dip raw fish in chogochujang.
I bought gochujang and vinegar to make chogochujang.
Could I have some more chogochujang?
We serve blanched squid with chogochujang.
The chogochujang was too sour, so I added sugar.
Adding chogochujang to spicy noodles makes them tangy.

explain: 주로 회나 데친 해산물에 찍어 먹는 새콤달콤한 소스예요. 고기를 쌈에 싸 먹을 때 쓰는 '쌈장'과는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: It is a sweet-and-sour dipping sauce used mainly for raw fish and blanched seafood. It is used differently from '쌈장', which goes with meat wraps.

examples.en: We timed the running record with a stopwatch.
The teacher pressed the stopwatch.
Please reset the stopwatch to zero.
I installed a stopwatch app on my phone.

examples.ko: 경기 전에 초시계가 고장 나서 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: The stopwatch broke before the match, so I bought a new one.
Stop right away when the stopwatch beeps.

explain: 휴대폰이나 시계 기능에서는 '스톱워치'라는 말도 많이 써요. 시간을 재기 시작할 때는 '초시계를 누르다', 끝낼 때는 '멈추다'라고 해요.
explain_en: On phones and watch functions people also commonly say '스톱워치'. You say '초시계를 누르다' to start timing and '멈추다' to stop it.

examples.en: This painting sold for the highest price ever.
House prices rose and hit a record high.
The price of gold has passed its record high again.

examples.ko: 이 가게에서 가장 비싼 건 최고가 제품이에요.
examples.en: The most expensive item in this shop is the top-priced product.
I wanted to sell at the highest price, but it was not easy.

examples.ko: 주가가 올라 올해 최고가를 새로 썼어요.
examples.en: The stock price rose and set a new high for this year.

explain: 반대말은 '최저가'예요. 뉴스에서는 '최고가를 기록하다', '최고가를 경신하다'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is '최저가' (lowest price). In the news it often appears as '최고가를 기록하다' or '최고가를 경신하다' (to break the record).

examples.en: Try finding the maximum value of this function.
The maximum value on the graph is twelve.
I calculated the difference between the maximum and minimum values.

examples.ko: 엑셀에서 최댓값을 찾는 방법을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me how to find the maximum value in Excel.
The maximum temperature was reached yesterday afternoon.

examples.ko: 시험 점수 중 최댓값이 구십오 점이에요.
examples.en: The highest of the test scores is ninety-five.

explain: 반대말은 '최솟값'이에요. 수학, 엑셀, 통계에서 주로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '제일 높은 점수'처럼 풀어서 말해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '최솟값'. It is used mainly in math, Excel and statistics, while in everyday talk people say things like '제일 높은 점수' (the highest score).

examples.ko: 새 병원은 최신식 장비를 갖추고 있어요.
examples.en: The new hospital is equipped with the latest equipment.
That factory switched to state-of-the-art facilities.
It is a modern building, so the facilities are very clean.

examples.ko: 최신식 주방이 있는 집으로 이사하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to move to a house with a modern kitchen.
Our school library is completely up to date.

examples.ko: 최신식이라고 해서 꼭 좋은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being the latest does not necessarily mean it is good.

explain: 주로 '최신식 장비', '최신식 건물'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여서 써요. 반대말은 '구식'이에요. 휴대폰이나 자동차 같은 제품에는 '최신형'이 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It is mostly used before a noun, as in '최신식 장비' or '최신식 건물'. The opposite is '구식'. For products like phones and cars, '최신형' often sounds more natural.

examples.en: The final decision will be announced tomorrow.
The boss makes the final judgment on this matter.
I am waiting for the final result.
The ultimate responsibility lies with the team leader.
After the interview, I finally passed.
I will do the final check.

explain: 실제로는 '최종적으로', '최종적인'으로 훨씬 많이 쓰고, '최종적 + 명사'는 글에서 볼 수 있어요. 말할 때는 '최종 결정'처럼 '최종'만 붙이는 게 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: In practice it is far more common as '최종적으로' or '최종적인', and '최종적 + noun' is seen mostly in writing. In speech, just '최종' as in '최종 결정' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 마라톤 참가자들은 아침 일곱 시까지 출발선에 모여 주세요.
examples.en: Marathon participants, please gather at the starting line by seven in the morning.
I waited for the signal at the starting line.
It is a foul if you cross the starting line.
The children stood side by side in front of the starting line.
My heart pounded when I stood at the starting line.

examples.ko: 모두 출발선 뒤로 한 발 물러나세요.
examples.en: Everyone, please step back behind the starting line.

explain: 반대는 '결승선'이에요. 달리기뿐 아니라 사람이 시작하는 조건을 비유할 때도 써요. '출발선이 다르다'는 처음부터 조건이 불공평하다는 말로 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 집안 형편이 달라서 출발선이 다르다는 말이 나와요.
phrases.en: People say we do not start from the same line because our family situations differ.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람마다 처음 가진 조건이 달라 공정하지 않다는 느낌으로 써요. 사회 문제를 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say people begin with unequal conditions, implying unfairness. It often comes up when discussing social issues.
phrases.en_equiv: not start on a level playing field

explain_en: The opposite is '결승선' (finish line). Besides races, it is used figuratively for the conditions people start with. '출발선이 다르다' often means the starting conditions are unfair from the beginning.

examples.en: The teacher opens the roll book and calls out names.
My name is not in the attendance book.
Please stamp the attendance book.
I took the roll book to the staff room.
Looking at the roll book, I have three absences.

examples.ko: 출석부 때문에 지각 기록이 그대로 남았어요.
examples.en: The attendance book kept my record of being late.

explain: 선생님이 이름을 부르며 확인하는 걸 '출석을 부르다'라고 해요. 확인하는 일 자체는 '출석 체크'라고도 해요.
explain_en: When a teacher calls names to check, it is called '출석을 부르다'. The act itself is also called '출석 체크'.
